title: Judgment service
description: /data/config/judgment.yaml. Typed, calibrated answers from an external service, used where deterministic code has to make a semantic call. Advisory everywhere: a judgment may reorder evidence and divide the context budget, and may never accept work, reject work, or widen a refusal. Absent file means disabled, which is the shipped state.

enabled.description: Required. Six registered sites can change control flow and are answered by this service, so a task cannot run without it. Disabling this leaves those decisions unmakeable rather than defaulted.

model.description: Required when enabled. Pin a concrete version such as jev-1.13.0 rather than a moving alias: the model id is part of the judgment cache key and of every benchmark's provenance, so an alias makes two runs incomparable while the configuration looks unchanged. `bcode judgment smoke` confirms the service accepts it.

api_key_env.description: The name of an environment variable holding the key. The name, never the value, so this file stays safe to commit and to attach to a bug report.

redact.description: strict sends no repository source: the objective, paths, symbol names, kinds, line ranges and counts only. repo_text additionally permits signatures and short excerpts, subject to the egress-sensitive path check and the credential scan, and bcode doctor names the mode on every run.

min_confidence.description: The floor for choice and score answers where a call site sets none of its own. Below it the deterministic answer stands. It does not apply to yes/no questions, which report no separate confidence.

timeout_seconds.description: Bounds one request. Zero or absent means 20 seconds. A slow judge is treated as an absent one.

cache.description: Store answers content-addressed by state, model and question set, so a repeated question costs nothing.

allOf.$comment: The loader refuses an enabled configuration with no model, because the model id is part of the judgment cache key: without one, a cached answer cannot be tied to what produced it. The schema has to refuse it too, or an editor would call a file valid that the program then rejects.
